summary: Discovery for Redwood Dedicated capacity. Lighthouse Capital is evaluating reserved GPU pools for inference of their risk-modeling LLMs. Main concerns: isolation/data residency, burst handling, autoscaling/throughput expectations, encryption/KMS, and pricing/commit levels. Redwood AE+SE discussed Dedicated architecture, private deployment options, and pilot steps.
transcript:
00:00 Tom Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Tom from Redwood, this is Maya our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Daniel Park: Good, thanks. Sorry running a little late, had back-to-back.
00:10 Tom Reed: No worries. Quick agenda: understand your workload, talk about dedicated/reserved capacity options, isolation and security, burst/scale, and next steps.
00:22 Sara Lopez: Awesome. High level, we're running internal risk models and a customer-facing assistant that scores loan requests. Latency target is sub-200ms P95 for short prompts, and throughput spikes at month-end. We're evaluating Dedicated because we need isolation and predictable cost.
00:40 Maya Chen: Got it. Can you give rough qps and model sizes?
00:45 Sara Lopez: Most inference is a mix — a 7B-ish open model for fast stuff and a 70B variant for high-fidelity scoring. Right now baseline is 60 qps steady, spikes up to ~400 qps for 10-12 hours at month end.
01:02 Alex Rivera: And we have strict network egress policies, all traffic must come from our VPC peered networks; we also need customer-managed KMS for keys.
01:12 Tom Reed: Perfect — that maps well to our Dedicated and Private options. Quick clarification: when you say Dedicated, are you looking for Redwood-managed Dedicated in our cloud region with isolated GPU pools, or fully private in your VPC/on-prem?
01:24 Daniel Park: Prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated in our cloud account or a VPC peered setup, because we don't want to manage the stack but need control over networking and keys.
01:33 Maya Chen: Okay. Our Dedicated offering provisions reserved GPU pools tied to your account, with network isolation and optional VPC peering. For KMS we support customer KMS via key grants, or bring-your-own HSM if required. There's also a Private deployment for on-prem or fully customer-controlled control plane.
01:52 Sara Lopez: For monthly spikes, do you support burst capacity? We don't want to overcommit and pay for peak full time.
01:59 Maya Chen: Yes. Our Dedicated model supports baseline reserved capacity plus a burst pool. You can reserve a commit for predictable throughput and allow burst-on-demand to scale above commit. Burst is subject to regional availability and is billed at short-term premium rates. We can set policys for burst preemption, fallback models, and can route lower-critical requests to cheaper model variants during spikes.
02:21 Alex Rivera: How predictable is latency when bursting? We can't have huge tail latencies during spikes.
02:26 Maya Chen: The runtime favors low-latency by default: continuous batching and KV cache optimizations. For bursts, you'll see slight increases at the P95 tails depending on queuing, but we can configure reserved lanes for high-priority routes to hold latency SLOs. Also model quantization recommendations help reduce token latencies.
02:45 Daniel Park: What about isolation? If we have regulated data, we need tenant isolation and audit logs.
02:50 Tom Reed: Dedicated gives you GPU isolation and data plane separation; logs are delivered to your SIEM or retained per contract. We provide audit logs, per-request tracing, and we've done SOC 2 customers. We'll share the SOC 2 and ISO material.
03:05 Sara Lopez: Is there an option for on-prem later if compliance needs tighten?
03:09 Maya Chen: Yes, Private is the option — you run the inference runtime in your environment, either via a customer-managed control plane or an on-prem appliance. You can migrate from Redwood Managed Dedicated to Private with exportable configs. There is some work in networking and key rotation but we support it.
03:23 Alex Rivera: Latency to our app is important — how do you handle WAN hops for KV cache and cache warming?
03:29 Maya Chen: We do prefix/KV caching tailored per-tenant and keep warmers for common prompts. For multi-region setups we can colocate Dedicated pools to reduce egress; otherwise cold-starts for large KV caches can add a few hundred ms initially.
03:44 Daniel Park: Pricing — we need some numbers. Is there a sample TCO for a commit that handles 100 qps baseline with 2x burst?
03:51 Tom Reed: We'll send a TCO spreadsheet. Quick note — commit sizes map to GPU counts and model mix; we typically show cost per token and amortized infra. But baseline + burst is common pattern.
04:04 Sara Lopez: On the security side, we need SSO (SAML), RBAC, and fine-grained audit trails.
04:10 Tom Reed: All supported. SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls, and per-user audit trails. We also integrate with customer KMS.
04:18 Maya Chen: Also note we can enforce model whitelists per route and do model verifications for code-execution or function-calling.
04:27 Daniel Park: Any major limitations on model sizes or custom weights? We'd like to bring tuned 70B weights.
04:33 Maya Chen: We onboard custom weights regularly; largest constraint is VRAM/quantization. For 70B we recommend a quantized variant or sharded serving on multiple GPUs. We can propose 2-4 GPU shards depending on latency needs.
04:50 Alex Rivera: What's the SLA and uptime on Dedicated?
04:54 Tom Reed: SLA tiers available — typically 99.9% for Dedicated with incident SLAs. For Private/on-prem, uptime is customer-managed but we offer support SLAs.
05:03 Sara Lopez: For the pilot, we want to run a benchmark with our model and traffic pattern. How detailed is the benchmark?
05:10 Maya Chen: We provide a benchmark harness that can replay traffic, measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput, and cost per token. We'll need a sample model or model artifact, prompts, and a sample traffic distribution.
05:22 Daniel Park: How long does pilot provisioning take?
05:25 Tom Reed: For Redwood-managed Dedicated it's typically 3-5 business days for initial environment and a week to stabilize depending on quota approvals. For Private/on-prem it's longer — a few weeks for on-site work.
05:36 Sara Lopez: Any hidden bandwidth or egress costs?
05:38 Tom Reed: Egress depends on cloud region and your contract; we'll include estimates in TCO. For Private we avoid cloud egress if fully on-prem.
05:46 Daniel Park: Are there reference customers in financial services who've done Dedicated with you?
05:50 Tom Reed: Yes, we can share references — SMB and enterprise banks that use Dedicated for scoring and chat. We'll include a short reference list.
05:58 Alex Rivera: Regarding key management — our security team wants BYOK with HSM. Is that supported?
06:03 Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer KMS integration and can work on HSM integrations; there are some additional attestation steps.
06:10 Sara Lopez: For scaling, what's the autoscaling granularity? Seconds? Minutes?
06:14 Maya Chen: Autoscaling operates at seconds-to-minutes granularity for request-level routing and at minutes-to-hours for adding or removing GPU nodes. We recommend a hybrid pattern: request routing + baseline autoscale + burst pool.
06:28 Daniel Park: If burst capacity isn't available regionally, what happens?
06:31 Maya Chen: We fallback to preconfigured policies: either queue with backpressure, fall back to cheaper model variant, or redirect to another region if latency allows. We can configure priority queues per route.
06:43 Sara Lopez: How do you measure cost during pilot vs production?
06:46 Tom Reed: We'll provide token-level cost breakdowns, per-model and per-route cost metrics, and sample reports. Those appear in the console and we can share CSVs.
06:56 Alex Rivera: Anything special about network peering? Support for Transit Gateways?
07:00 Maya Chen: Yes, we support peering and TGW for AWS. We also support private endpoints. We'll coordinate networking details during pilot.
07:10 Daniel Park: Any concerns about model drift or regression during rollouts? We need eval hooks.
07:15 Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize has eval monitoring; we can tie regression alerts to prompt sets and block rollouts if quality drops.
07:23 Sara Lopez: What about developer ergonomics? SDKs, streaming?
07:26 Tom Reed: Full SDKs, streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured outputs supported.
07:33 Daniel Park: Perfect. Let's talk next steps.
07:35 Tom Reed: Action items: we'll send pricing/TCO, benchmark scripts, SOC 2 docs, and sample reference list. Proposed pilot week of 2026-03-16.
07:45 Maya (Data Scientist): Quick question — what's the recommended quantization for 70B?
07:48 Maya Chen: We normally recommend 4-bit or 5-bit quantization depending on tolerance; we can run accuracy checks during the benchmark.
07:56 Daniel Park: OK that's helpful. Any blockers on our side? Alex: we'll get GPU inventory and network constraints and share with Maya.
08:05 Tom Reed: Great. We'll follow up with an email and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.
08:12 Daniel Park: Thanks, talk soon.
